take_homes: Start with one agent. Split only when the access, the dialect or the stance differs, and test whether one prompt would do.
Work goes wrong at the handoffs between agents. When I look at an agent setup, I look at the seams first.
The output may be confidently wrong, and nothing in the module checks that. I check it myself.

monday.move: Nothing on my own. Maybe ask one analyst whether the three-retriever search could be run on a real market question, and compare the result with what we already know.
monday.who: one analyst from my team, if anyone has time
monday.when: sometime in the next two weeks, after the steering group
monday.stop_condition: The result is not clearly better than what the analyst produces alone, or it needs more than an hour of my time.
monday.blocker: My calendar, and my doubt about whether I could verify the output.

misconception.why: The course told me not to overuse its own method and said openly that nothing in it checks whether the answer is true. The last programmes never did that. The parallel retrieval is also something concrete I could not have had two years ago. I am not convinced it will last, but wait-and-see now looks a little less safe.

one_line: Less hype than I expected. They admit that one agent is often enough and that nobody checks whether the answer is true, which is more candour than the last three programmes gave me.
